scams.name: Porta Nuova Station & Freccia-Train Pickpockets
scams.description: Coordinated pickpocket crews work Verona Porta Nuova — Verona's day-tripper arrival hub from Milan, Venice and Bologna — and the Milano-Venezia Frecciarossa/Frecciabianca corridor that runs through it. L'Arena documents credit-card theft rings on Freccia trains whose stolen cards were used for same-day shopping; a February 2026 TgVerona/Telenuovo report records Polizia di Stato arrests in the Porta Nuova piazzale; L'Arena's 'Porta Nuova sotto assedio' series tracks 2–4 year sentences for the station gang. A traveler forum post documents a backpack stolen from a Milano–Verona Frecciarossa overhead rack. Add the Polfer-documented platform theft pattern — crews brush past you at the train door, open outer luggage zippers, and exit before the station stop ends.
scams.avoidance: Exit Porta Nuova through the main Piazzale XXV Aprile entrance onto the ATV bus rank, not through the back parking side. Keep luggage on the facing end-of-carriage rack on Frecciarossa/Italo, never the overhead rack above your head. Store wallet and phone in zipped internal pockets before the train pulls in. Never accept unsolicited ticket-machine 'help' — use the Trenitalia or Italo app only. Walk with your bag between your body and the platform wall, and treat any 'scusi' approach from a stranger in the station as hostile. If robbed, call 112 and state 'sono stato derubato in stazione.'
scams.location: Verona Porta Nuova station (platforms, underground passages, Piazzale XXV Aprile), Milano–Venezia Frecciarossa/Frecciabianca corridor, ATV bus rank

scams.name: Casa di Giulietta Courtyard Shakedowns (Bracelet + Fake Balcony Fee)
scams.description: Via Cappello 23 is the most-visited single address in Verona, and from April 1, 2026 the courtyard is ticketed — Repubblica reports a €5 entry fee introduced that date, following a €12 trial from December 2025 that triggered a Comune emergency review. Scammers exploit the fee transition three ways: friendship-bracelet hawkers tie a string on your wrist as you queue and demand €10–€20; fake 'balcony viewing fee' upsells are added to the real €5 courtyard ticket by touts working the Via Cappello entrance; and third-party resale sites (italy-museum.com lists it at €9, above the real municipal fee) take a markup on the now-standard entry. A traveler forum thread calls the balcony 'a tourist trap as much as Sherlock Holmes grave' — the balcony itself was a 1930s addition. Multiple VeronaSera cronaca reports document Via Mazzini (the pedestrian axis between Piazza Bra and Casa di Giulietta) as a pickpocket corridor — a November 2019 Zara-store arrest of a 30-year-old foreign woman caught with stolen goods is one of many.
scams.avoidance: Buy the €5 Casa di Giulietta courtyard ticket only at the official municipal ticket desk at Via Cappello 23 or on visitverona.it — never from a tout in the queue or a third-party resale site. Refuse anyone who moves to tie a string or bracelet on your wrist — step back, say 'no grazie,' and keep hands in pockets; the sunk-cost demand for €20 starts after the knot is tied. The balcony viewing is included in the courtyard ticket and there is no separate 'balcony fee.' Walk Via Mazzini with your bag on the shop-window side and zipper facing your body. Skip italy-museum.com, GetYourGuide, and other resale links at the top of Google — they add €4+ per ticket.
scams.location: Casa di Giulietta courtyard (Via Cappello 23), Via Cappello entrance queue, Via Mazzini pedestrian corridor, Piazza delle Erbe banchetti

scams.name: Arena Opera Festival Fake-Ticket Resellers
scams.description: Fondazione Arena di Verona (arena.it) is the only authorized ticket seller for the Arena Opera Festival. A January 14, 2020 VeronaSera report documents the Carabinieri di Vedelago arresting a 27-year-old woman from Naples for selling fake Arena concert tickets online. A TripAdvisor Verona Forum thread titled 'opera tickets - problems buying online' records a £350 credit-card charge from a non-official 'Arena tickets' seller that was never followed by seat numbers or confirmation. A community thread asks whether ticketsarenaverona.com is legitimate — a user notes the tickets did work but were cheaper than Fondazione Arena, suggesting unauthorized inventory or upstream cancellation risk. A parallel Opera Discoclub Bussolengo case (VeronaSera 2021) saw oversold tickets for a venue with ~600 capacity. Scalpers also work Piazza Bra on performance nights selling 'Category 1' tickets at markup — tickets that may be counterfeits or stolen QR codes already scanned elsewhere.
scams.avoidance: Buy Arena Opera Festival tickets only from arena.it (Fondazione Arena di Verona, via Roma 7d) — this is the single authorized channel and the only one eligible for refund via the official Guida Compilazione Rimborso. Avoid 'ticketsarena…,' 'arenaverona-tickets,' and any domain that isn't arena.it. Never buy printed tickets from a scalper on Piazza Bra on performance nights — scanned QR codes become worthless at the second scan. For the steps above the numbered seats (unnumbered gradinata) arrive 2+ hours early and bring a cushion; there is no need for a 'skip-the-line opera pass' from a third-party reseller. If a charge goes through without seat confirmation, file a chargeback immediately and contact Fondazione Arena's box office at +39 045 800 5151.
scams.location: Arena di Verona (Piazza Bra 1), Piazza Bra scalper zone on performance nights, Fondazione Arena box office (via Roma 7d)

scams.name: Finti Sordomute Petition Scam on Piazza Bra & Via Mazzini
scams.description: Teams of women pretending to be deaf-mute approach tourists on Piazza Bra, Via Mazzini, and Piazza delle Erbe carrying clipboards with petitions for fake charities ('Handicap International' is the most common name). Once you sign, they demand a donation — typically €10–€20 per signature — while a partner picks your pocket or bag. A Polizia di Stato di Verona press release (questure.poliziadistato.it) documents four Romanian women denounced for simulating a charity fundraiser. L'Arena documents multiple waves of arrests of 'finte sorde' in Piazza Bra ('Denunciate le tre finte sorde in azione in Bra' — already fined in prior months); a 2016 L'Arena story adds cases around Lake Garda ('Handicap International' ID). A traveler forum Verona post describes a traveler's younger brother being approached by two women who 'unfortunately was deaf' with a petition, exactly matching the Polizia di Stato case.
scams.avoidance: Never sign anything handed to you on Piazza Bra, Via Mazzini or Piazza delle Erbe — there is no legitimate Italian charity that solicits signatures on the street for cash. If approached with a clipboard and a sign-language gesture, say 'no' firmly and walk away without breaking stride. Do not reach for your wallet or bag while engaged. Keep hands on your bag whenever you stop to look at Piazza delle Erbe market stalls — the banchetti were fined €28k in May 2019 per Corriere del Veneto for selling counterfeits, and the same foot traffic attracts the petition crews. Report aggressive approaches to the Polizia Locale tourist desk on Piazza Bra.
scams.location: Piazza Bra, Via Mazzini, Piazza delle Erbe (market stalls), Ponte Pietra, Arena perimeter

scams.name: Abusivi Centurioni Photo Shakedown at the Arena
scams.description: Men in low-budget Roman-centurion costumes work the perimeter of the Arena and Piazza Bra, offering to pose for photos and then demanding €20 per shot. A VeronaOggi report dated June 21, 2023 documents polizia locale ejecting centurioni abusivi from in front of the Arena after they demanded €20 per tourist photo. A separate L'Arena report documents a sanctioned 'centurione' (Tiberghien operation) whose costume, Roman helmet replica, and sword were all seized by polizia locale — 34 verbali were issued against the usual accattoni operating in the same zone. The scam is quieter than Rome's Colosseum version because Verona's polizia locale has been aggressive about enforcement, but the costumes reappear seasonally, especially before Arena Opera Festival performances when tourist density on Piazza Bra peaks.
scams.avoidance: Do not pose with anyone in costume on Piazza Bra or the Arena perimeter — there is no legitimate fee-based photo-with-centurion service authorized by the Comune di Verona. If a costumed figure steps into your frame or your group photo, wave them away before shutter release. Never hand cash for a photo you didn't commission. If someone demands €20 after an unsolicited photo, walk away — the sanction is on them, not on you, and the polizia locale mobile unit patrols the piazza and can be flagged from the Arena ticket office. Compose Arena photos from the Ponte della Vittoria side of Piazza Bra for the cleanest wide-angle without centurion traffic.
scams.location: Arena di Verona perimeter (Piazza Bra), Ponte della Vittoria, Liston passeggiata

scams.name: Piazza Bra / Liston Restaurant Tourist-Menu Trap
scams.description: The Liston — Piazza Bra's curved restaurant strip facing the Arena — combines Verona's highest rent per square meter with the city's densest opera-going tourist flow, and the bill pattern matches. Unmarked €3–€5 per-person coperto, 12–15% 'servizio' applied automatically on foreign cards, fish or bistecca alla fiorentina priced 'al etto' (per 100g) that arrives at 400–600g, house-wine mark-ups of 3–4x the bottle's supermarket price, and 'pane e acqua' or amaro digestivi added without consent. A TripAdvisor Ristorante Caffè Vittorio Emanuele (Piazza Bra 16) review typifies the complaint pattern. Corriere del Veneto's May 2019 report on Piazza Erbe banchetti (€28k in municipal-police fines on market stalls for tourist overcharging and counterfeits) underscores the enforcement reality — the problem is known and fined, but Piazza Bra turnover keeps it fresh.
scams.avoidance: Walk 3–5 minutes off the Liston — Via Sottoriva, Via Mazzanti, Piazzetta Navona and the streets behind Castelvecchio all have authentic Veronese osterias charging half of Piazza Bra prices. Photograph the menu posted outside the restaurant before sitting — Italian law requires prices to be posted publicly, and the fish/steak price per etto must be there. At seating, ask 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?' Refuse any unrequested pane, antipasti or amaro. For Amarone or Valpolicella wine, request the bottle price before ordering — Liston mark-ups on house wines are legal but often shocking. Trust Italian-language Google reviews sorted by Most Recent over English reviews.
scams.location: Liston curve of Piazza Bra, Via Mazzini restaurant cluster, Piazza delle Erbe cafe terraces

scams.name: Airport Catullo Taxi Overcharge & A4 Finti Poliziotti Auto Civetta
scams.description: Two distinct transport scams cluster around arrival into Verona. First, taxis at Aeroporto Valerio Catullo (Villafranca) — a Corriere del Veneto 2026 report documents one tassista suspended for queue-jumping and abusing colleagues at the Catullo rank, and a 2025 Verona news Instagram post documents a €40+ charge for a 1.6km Catullo-area ride. The Aerobus airport shuttle from Catullo to Porta Nuova is €8 and takes 15 minutes. Second, A4 autostrada 'auto civetta' scams: VeronaSera documents bands using unmarked cars and fake police badges (tesserini falsi) to pretend to be plainclothes officers, stopping tourists on the Milan–Venice A4 through Verona's territory and demanding 'fine payments' or ID checks — Corriere Brescia and a 2013 Garda case document the same Lake Garda A4 pattern. A related ZTL (limited-traffic-zone) cascade: a 2023 traveler scams forum post documents an Avis rental car in Verona generating 5 post-trip emails for bus-lane/ZTL fines that Italian municipalities forward to rental companies months later.
scams.avoidance: Skip the Catullo taxi rank entirely — take the Aerobus (€8, stops every 20 min, ticket from the driver or catullo.it) to Porta Nuova, then walk 15 minutes to Piazza Bra. If you must use a taxi, confirm the approximate fare before closing the door (Catullo-to-center is normally €35–€40 meter-on). On the A4 autostrada, never pull over for an unmarked car — real Polizia Stradale uses marked Alfa Romeo Giulia sedans in blue-white livery and wears full uniform; demand to proceed to the nearest Polizia Stradale station if a plainclothes 'officer' signals you over. If renting, photograph the dashboard odometer and every ZTL sign near the rental pickup — Verona's historic-center ZTL is heavily cameraed and fines arrive 6+ months after return.
scams.location: Aeroporto Valerio Catullo (Villafranca), A4 autostrada Milan–Venezia through Verona province, Verona historic-center ZTL, Garda/Lazise/Bussolengo A4 exits
